Common Eider eggs incubate for about 24–26 days.
Female Common Eiders often reuse their nesting site from the previous year.
King Eiders nest in Arctic tundra near lakes or ocean coasts.
King Eiders can raise ducklings in freshwater or saltwater habitats.
King Eiders can collect prey from the underside of sea ice.
King Eiders eat starfish as well as shellfish and crustaceans.
King Eiders can dabble for food in shallow freshwater.
Young King Eiders typically spend their first summer at sea.
A King Eider clutch can contain 2–7 eggs.
